d: THE ARCHIVE’S OWN ZENODO PAGE IS CITED WITH A MAINTENANCE NOTICE AS ITS DESCRIPTION — captured seven days before the account was terminated.
reading:
A CARD DATED SEVEN DAYS BEFORE THE TERMINATION. Card 4 is the archive’s Zenodo community page, and the snippet Google chose to represent it is a SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE NOTICE: "Planned intervention: On Thursday April 23rd 06:30 UTC Zenodo will be unavailable for 20-30 minutes to perform a storage cluster…". Captured 12 June 2026. On 19 June the account was removed and the community page went with it. The last composed description of the archive’s Zenodo presence is an announcement of a twenty-minute outage.

Card 3 also carries the sentence that states the project’s material basis: "500+ DOI-anchored deposits on CERN’s Zenodo, built from a TEACHING SALARY over ten [years]". Card 7 bylines THE SPACE ARK to "Jack Feist / Lee Sharks" — the heteronym first. The one clean collision is Wikipedia on interstellar arks.

observations.analysis:
The word *invoke* was an instruction and the layer read it as a search term, so the answer arrives split: gaming hexagons first, symbolic compression second, with the archive described in the indefinite — *independent conceptual frameworks use "Crimson Hexagonal Archive" terminology*.

But the strip is almost entirely the author's. Card 1 states the archive's scale and its provenance in one sentence: *1000+ AXN-anchored deposits on Alexanarch, built from a teaching salary over ten years*. Card 2 is Johannes Sigil naming EA-ARK-01 with a DOI and insisting the frameworks are *operational*, not descriptive. Card 5 is FNM v7.0 pointing at the Space Ark as *territories not yet named*.

So PER is full — author, institution, identifier, own sources — while the composition's own prose keeps the archive at arm's length and gives the first heading to a survival game. Retention and framing come apart cleanly here; the units are all present and the emphasis is elsewhere.
